source.title: Ischemic stroke mimics: A comprehensive review

extraction.secondary_source_guardrail: This source is a review article, not primary literature. Quantitative atoms represent the review’s own cross-study synthesis or are explicitly tagged secondary_reported_result; they must not be treated as primary-study observations.
extraction.batching_decision: Single-pass semantic extraction was used: the retrieved source is 9 pages and could be fully mapped, visually reconciled, atomized, and validated without context pressure.

coverage.supplement_status: Supplementary Table 1 is referenced in the article but no supplementary file was present in the retrieved Drive folder.

extraction_limitations: The ATOM schema is designed for primary literature; this document is a review article. Review-synthesized results are preserved with secondary-source tags and should not be mistaken for direct participant-level primary evidence.
The source reports pooled counts and percentages but does not describe a conventional meta-analytic model, weighting strategy, heterogeneity assessment, or risk-of-bias framework.
Many pooled outcomes use different contributing-study denominators, so atom populations are outcome-specific rather than one fixed cohort.
Supplementary Table 1 was not included among the raw Drive documents and therefore could not be atomized or reconciled.
Cited-study claims in the Discussion were not independently verified against the cited primary publications.
consistency_findings: The abstract reports stroke-mimic prevalence as 24.8% (15,044/60,703), while the main Results section reports 24.9% (15,595/62,664). Both assertions are preserved rather than reconciled.
The conclusion states that one out of three mimics is thrombolyzed, whereas the pooled Results estimate is 26.3% (635/2,407); the conclusion is therefore only an approximate characterization.

The main Results section states that 61 studies were selected, but its listed design counts (5 + 1 + 17 + 9 + 30) sum to 62; the source does not explain whether categories overlap or contain a counting error.
schema_gaps: No dedicated atom kind exists for secondary-review synthesis or review recommendations/workflows; tags are used to preserve that distinction.

QuantitativeResult stores one estimate plus optional arm observations, which is imperfect for multi-group review summaries that report only arm-level percentages and p-values without a formal effect estimate.

duplicate_review.within_set_duplicate_review: No intentional duplicate atoms; the abstract and main-text stroke-mimic prevalence atoms are retained separately because the source reports conflicting values.
